title: The Cartesian plane
log: 2026-11-20T12:15:19Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: The closest bank point covers plotting (x, y) points and the four quadrants, but it never teaches naming a quadrant from the signs of the coordinates, which the new point requires, and adding that step would change the card rather than adjust it.

draft.title: The Cartesian plane
card: The Cartesian plane has a horizontal x-axis and a vertical y-axis. They cross at the origin, \((0, 0)\).
A point is written \((x, y)\). Go across first (right is positive, left is negative). Then go up or down (up is positive, down is negative).
The axes split the plane into four quadrants. Quadrant 1 is top right. Then go anticlockwise: quadrant 2 is top left, quadrant 3 is bottom left, quadrant 4 is bottom right.
The signs of the coordinates name the quadrant. For example, \((-4, 3)\) has a negative \(x\) and a positive \(y\), so it is in quadrant 2.

2.alt: A Cartesian plane with the point \((3, -2)\) marked. It is 3 units right of the origin and 2 units below the x-axis.

draft.remember: Write \((x, y)\): across first, then up or down. The signs tell you the quadrant.

a.q: Which point is 5 units to the left of the origin and 2 units up?
a.why: Left is negative for \(x\) and up is positive for \(y\), and \(x\) is written first, so the point is \((-5, 2)\). \((-2, 5)\) is tempting but swaps the order of the coordinates.
a.clue: Across comes first, and left is negative.

b.q: Mia plots the point \((-6, -1)\) on a Cartesian plane. Which quadrant is it in?
b.why: Both coordinates are negative, so the point is left of the y-axis and below the x-axis. That is quadrant 3, the bottom left. Quadrant 2 is wrong because it needs a positive \(y\) value.
b.clue: Check the sign of each coordinate, then count anticlockwise from the top right.
